summary.text: Amy Mills is the Greens candidate for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in disability support, is a qualified dietitian, and has described herself as a renter who lives with ADHD and autism. She contested the federal seat of Deakin for the Greens in 2025, taking 11.9% of first preferences.

priorities.text: I'm running to help restore hope, push for fair rent and homelessness prevention
Easing housing costs and the cost of living for local people
Better access to mental health care
Protecting Ringwood's environment, including its tree canopy and public spaces, as climate risks grow
Spending public money where it does most for community wellbeing

sources.title: Ringwood: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Amy Mills, Candidate for Ringwood, Australian Greens

summary.text: Christopher William Norton, listed by the ABC as Christopher Norton, is the Labour DLP candidate for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Neither the ABC nor the party had published a biography of him as at 9 Nov 2026, and the party's website was not serving any pages when checked.

summary.text: Jack Gardner is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian election. He works as a bartender while studying at Deakin University, and at 19 was elected a union delegate at Australia Post. Locally he has campaigned against the Borral Quarry in Montrose and for shutting weapons manufacturers in Melbourne's east.

priorities.text: Justice for Palestine
Higher pay and secure housing for working people
Opposing the far right
Keeping public spaces in Ringwood out of private hands

summary.text: John O'Connor is One Nation's candidate for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he spent more than 33 years with Victoria Police, and that his later jobs include patient transport, private investigation and delivery driving. According to the same profile, he is a former Army Reservist and has helped lead local football clubs.

occupation.text: Patient transport, private investigation and delivery driving, after a career with Victoria Police

priorities.text: Giving animal protection more attention in Parliament
Stronger environmental protection, including for local bushland and wildlife
Policy based on research and evidence

summary.text: Lyndon Walker is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The party describes him as a Ringwood-based researcher and educator with a doctorate in statistics and sociology, whose career has been mainly in the health and education sectors. He is a director of the Tangaroa Blue Foundation, which works on marine debris, and a member of Maroondah's environmental advisory committee.

summary.text: Nick McGowan has been a Liberal member of the Legislative Council for North-Eastern Metropolitan Region since the 2022 election, and is Shadow Minister for Environment and for Fire Rescue Victoria. Before Parliament he worked for the United Nations, sat on the Migration and Refugee Review Tribunals, and was chief of staff to Matthew Guy. He is reported to be standing for the Assembly seat of Ringwood in 2026 rather than for the Council; neither his Parliament page nor Wikipedia confirms the move.

summary.text: Prue Cutts is running as an independent for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian election, endorsed by the Voices of Deakin community group. She has sat on Whitehorse City Council since 2016 and has twice been deputy mayor. Her earlier career was in teaching, careers counselling and vocational psychology, and she has run a small business.

occupation.text: Teacher, careers counsellor and vocational psychologist; small business owner

prior_roles.note: The ABC says she served two one-year terms as deputy mayor between 2022 and 2025; it does not give the exact years.

prior_roles.role: Chair of the Community Safety, Health and Wellbeing, and Arts and Culture committees

priorities.text: Stronger integrity laws and more power for IBAC, the Ombudsman and the Auditor-General
A full rebuild of Maroondah Hospital on a new site, plus an urgent care clinic in Ringwood
More frequent Belgrave and Lilydale line trains and better local bus links
Scrapping the Activity Centre program and restoring third-party planning appeals
More social and affordable housing near transport, and stronger protections for renters

summary.text: Rachel Halse is Labor's candidate for Ringwood at the 2026 Victorian election. She is an emergency nurse working in the area and previously worked in policy for the nurses' union, the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Federation (Victoria). She is married to Dustin Halse, Labor's member for Ringwood from 2018 to 2022.

prior_roles.organisation: Australian Nursing and Midwifery Federation (Victorian Branch)

priorities.text: Keeping cost-of-living help for families, such as free kindergarten, free travel on public transport for under-18s and power bill bonuses
Good, accessible health care, drawing on her work as a frontline nurse
Securing better local services for Ringwood
